result.summary: The street environment is primarily car-oriented, featuring a narrow sidewalk on only one side of the road with no buffer from moving traffic. The opposite side lacks a paved walkway entirely, and there are no marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures visible within the frame.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: The right side of the street lacks a paved sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to walk on unpaved surfaces or in the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks visible, which increases risk for pedestrians attempting to cross the two-lane road.

hazards.name: Narrow Sidewalk without Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is narrow and lacks any physical buffer (like a planting strip) from the travel lane.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk on the right side of the street to ensure a safe path for pedestrians on both sides.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility continental crosswalks and curb ramps to provide designated and safer crossing points.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a two-lane roadway with a single, narrow sidewalk on the far side, bordered by a chain-link fence and a grassy embankment. The pedestrian environment lacks a walkway on the near side and features obstructions like a large tree and utility poles that narrow the existing path.

hazards.description: There is no sidewalk on the near side of the street, forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway or cross without a marked facility.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large tree and utility pole are located immediately adjacent to or within the narrow sidewalk path, reducing the effective width for pedestrians and those with mobility aids.

interventions.title: New Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install a paved sidewalk on the near side of the street to provide a continuous and safe walking environment for pedestrians on both sides.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Widen the existing sidewalk on the far side to meet accessibility standards and provide a clear path around fixed obstructions like trees and poles.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a sidewalk on only one side of the street, with residential housing facing a fenced park area. The roadway is in poor condition with significant patching and lacks marked crossings or traffic calming, though a dedicated bike lane is present.

result.summary: A residential street lined with row houses featuring a continuous but narrow sidewalk directly adjacent to the curb. The environment lacks pedestrian safety enhancements such as buffers, street lighting, or traffic calming measures, relying on the low-volume nature of the street for safety.

hazards.description: The narrow sidewalk is located directly against the curb with no planting strip or furniture zone to separate pedestrians from moving traffic.

hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street creates sightline obstructions between drivers and pedestrians.
